_about: media-optimizer does NOT read this file. It lists every setting with its built-in default.
To change settings, create ~/.config/media-optimizer/config.json (or pass --config FILE,
or set MO_CONFIG) with only the keys you want to change. Keys starting with an
underscore are comments. Every key can also be set as an environment variable
_max_workers: Parallel workers for images, GIFs, AVIF and checks. null = number of CPU cores.
_delete_original: Move originals to the trash after a verified conversion. null = follow the mode: true in place, false with a target directory.
_rename_inplace: In place, rename 'name_h265.mp4' back to 'name.mp4' once the original is gone. null = follow the mode like delete_original.
_force_delete: If the trash fails, delete permanently without asking.
_include_hidden: Also process hidden files and folders. Trash and NAS system folders are always skipped.
_verify_deep: Fully decode every image output before accepting it (slower).
_preflight: Before the run, correct file extensions that do not match the content (in place only).
_use_cache: Remember files that need no work next time: finished videos, and results without an output (discarded as larger, unsupported, not selected). Each stage has its own cache file; entries store size, modification time and the settings they depend on. false = check everything again.
_log_file: Path of the run log. null = media-optimizer.log in the project folder (checkout) or the state folder (installed).
_log_max_kb: The log is renamed to .log.1 at the start of a run once it is larger than this.
_img_target: Target format for JPEG and PNG. jxl keeps JPEG bit-exact; webp re-encodes JPEG lossily.
_img_discard_if_larger: Discard an image result that is not smaller than the original.
_img_copy_metadata: Copy PNG metadata with exiftool. auto = when installed, always = refuse to start without it.
_jxl_effort: cjxl effort, higher is slower and smaller.
_png_quality: JXL quality for PNG with png_mode lossy.
_cjxl_threads: Threads per cjxl process. 1 avoids N workers x N threads.
_gif_target: webp is lossless, avif about half the size but lossy.
_gif_kmin: Minimum keyframe distance in animated WebP. 0 = no keyframes, smallest files.
_discard_if_larger: Discard a GIF, clip or video result that is not smaller than the original.
_clip_stage: Run the clip stage (short silent videos to AVIF or WebP) in a full run.
_clip_format: Format for short silent videos. avif is about a third of the size, but GNOME's image viewer (glycin 2.1, Fedora 44) shows only its first frame; webp animates everywhere, and is often larger than an H.264 source.
_clip_max_seconds: Only videos shorter than this go to the clip stage.
_clip_require_silent: Only videos without audio. Neither AVIF nor animated WebP can store sound.
_clip_source_codecs: Source codecs the clip stage accepts.
_clip_webp_quality_retry: Subtracted from the WebP quality for one more attempt when the result is too large.
_avif_crf: AV1 quality for clip_format avif, lower is better.
_avif_crf_retry: Added to the CRF for one more attempt when the result is too large.
_video_container: auto = mp4 for mp4/m4v/mov sources, mkv for the rest (MP4 cannot hold Opus or SRT).
_source_codecs: Source codecs that get re-encoded. HEVC, VP9 and AV1 are already efficient.
_encoder_mode: auto picks the GPU above the bitrate threshold or from gpu_min_pixels on.
_bitrate_threshold_kbps: In auto mode: below this bitrate the CPU encodes (better density).
_gpu_min_pixels: In auto mode the GPU always encodes from this frame size on. 0 disables it.
_gpu_workers: GPU encodes running at the same time; a CPU encode runs alongside in any case. Measured on an RX 9070 XT, six 1080p clips including the picture check: 1 = 17.6 s, 2 = 12.2 s, 3 = 10.9 s.
_vaapi_device: VAAPI render node, or auto to try them all.
_gpu_codec: GPU encoder. See gpu-selftest for what works on this machine.
_gpu_bf: Maximum B-frames on the GPU. null = ffmpeg decides.
_gpu_allow_10bit: Encode 10-bit sources in 10 bit on the GPU (p010 + main10).
_hevc_tag: Container tag such as hvc1. Empty = ffmpeg default. Check with gpu-selftest first.
_faststart: Move the MP4 index to the front.
_enable_probe: Encode short test slices first and skip videos that would not shrink enough.
_probe_margin_pct: Skip when the probe reaches this percentage of the original. 100 = only when it grows.
_probe_slices: Number of slices the test material is split into.
_keep_salvaged_corrupt: Keep a video salvaged from a damaged source even when it grew. The original is always kept.
_duration_tolerance_pct: Allowed runtime difference between original and output.
_auto_fix_list: Process only .broken_videos.txt from the target directory when it exists.
_verify_visual: Compare the picture of every video output with its source (PSNR samples).
_visual_psnr_min: Below this the picture counts as suspicious. Sound re-encodes measure 31-38 dB.
_visual_strict: Discard a suspicious video output instead of only warning.
_enable_verify_output: After a full run with a target directory, check every video output again.
_check_visual: The final check also compares pictures.
